about: Output of the legacy SQL function dbo.GetHargaObatNew_WithStok, run read-only on 13 November 2026 with (price group, 'xx', KTP, item, CustomerKerjasamaID 0, '', 0) by legacy-drug-prices.sql: KTP 1 in Kuta 1, Seroja, and Penta, and KTP 0 in Seroja and Penta for the same items. Master values and prices only, no patient data. Gradings are the SIMmGradingHargaObat rows of TipePelayanan STANDARD for each KTP value (ktp true is KTP 1); grading_group null would mean the legacy ALL rows (none in these sources).

Every case is fed to the pure price rule with conversion 1, its KTP, and the unit_price_decimals of its source, the pharmacy setting desimal_harga_satuan: Kuta 1 and Penta 0 (their copies return round(@HargaObat, 0)), Seroja 4 (its copy returns @HargaObat as money without round, which keeps four decimals). A case must give legacy_price unless it is listed in expected_differences, which states the price our rule gives and why.

seroja.database: Klinik Seroja (copy on the Penta dev server)

reasons.seroja-item-class: The Seroja copy also requires SIMmGradingHargaObat.KelasBarangID = mBarang.Kelas_ID. In Seroja's data every grading group equals the item's class name (ANTIBIOTIK ORAL, BHP, INJEKSI, OBAT ORAL, TOPIKAL; XX is class NONE, 700 items) except this one item of class ALKES placed in group XX; the legacy class key gives it 0 % because the XX rows are for class NONE only. This is a data inconsistency of that item, not a rule: when Seroja's data is ported, the item gets the grading group of its class (ALKES), and our rule then gives 0 % like legacy.

not_carried.reason: Decision 6: no service-type dimension. It is inert in every legacy copy: every lookup by TipePelayanan=@JenisLayanan that sets the markup or discount is commented out, and the live lookups use the literal 'STANDARD'. No case exercises it.

not_carried.rule: Guarantor contracts: CustomerKerjasamaID, ObatUp, guarantor category CC108 "MA", HargaObatDigunakan
not_carried.reason: They depend on hard-coded ids in the legacy function. The oracle passed CustomerKerjasamaID 0, so no case exercises them.

not_carried.rule: BPJS + Fornas items at base price
not_carried.reason: A BPJS grading row of 0 % expresses it as data. No source has a Fornas item (Penta 0 of 3.505).
Depends on a hard-coded class; not carried. No case exercises it.

It depends on a hard-coded id. A price group that should ignore KTP gets grading rows for both values, as data. In Seroja, BPJS with KTP 0 gives the base price either way: our rule finds no BPJS KTP 0 row (0 %), and legacy uses the BPJS KTP 1 row of 0 %.

unit_conversion.about: Legacy never sold in a unit other than the stock unit. With whole-rupiah rounding, ours rounds once after multiplying by the unit content (BC ConvertAmountByUnitOfMeasure), so a STRIP of 10 is not 10 x the rounded tablet price: 495 x 1.1 = 544.5 per tablet.

seroja_unit_conversion.about: With Seroja's four decimals nothing is rounded away: 84.38 x 1.3 = 109.694 per tablet, and a STRIP of 10 is exactly 10 x the tablet price.
